hints: Go through rows A, B and D first and tick off the ones you are 100% sure about, then look very carefully at the location claim in row C.
Ask yourself: in a eukaryotic cell, is DNA really only in the nucleus? Think about mitochondria (and chloroplasts in plants) and where RNA is made and used.
walkthrough:
**Recall the real RNA vs DNA differences**

Think structure first. RNA uses ribose sugar, uracil base, and is usually single stranded. DNA uses deoxyribose sugar, thymine base, and is usually double stranded.

That already tells you rows A, B and D look correct.

**Check the location claim in row C**

It is true that RNA is found throughout the cell, in the nucleus, cytoplasm, ribosomes and more. But is DNA found only in the nucleus?

No. Eukaryotic cells also have small circular DNA in mitochondria, and plants have it in chloroplasts too.

**Pick the mistaken row**

Since A, B and D are all true differences, the one mistake must be row C. The DNA side of row C is wrong because DNA is not only in the nucleus.

options.A: This row is correct, so it is not the mistake. RNA does contain ribose and DNA does contain deoxyribose.
options.B: This row is correct, so it is not the mistake. RNA uses uracil instead of thymine, while DNA uses thymine instead of uracil.
options.C: This is the mistake. RNA is found throughout the cell, but DNA is not only in the nucleus as it is also found in mitochondria and, in plants, chloroplasts.
options.D: This row is correct, so it is not the mistake. RNA is normally a single polynucleotide while DNA is normally two polynucleotides in a double helix.
